title: At the restaurant
goal: Order a real dinner, say what you like and don't like, and know Georgian cuisine well enough to order without pointing at the menu.
bekal: say მიყვარს (I love/like) and მომწონს (I like this)
name ten Georgian dishes that are sure to be on the menu
praise the food and ask for the bill

dialogs.title: დიალოგი — First khinkali
dialogs.intro: Ani, Nino, and Levan are having dinner at a khinkali restaurant. Notice the two different verbs for "like", and one eating tip that separates foreigners from people who've been taught.

lines.speaker: მიმტანი:
lines.id: Welcome! What would you like to order?

lines.speaker: ლევანი:
lines.id: Ten khinkali, one khachapuri, and a salad.
lines.literal: ten — khinkali, one — khachapuri — and — salad.

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: A bottle of red and a bottle of water.
lines.literal: one — bottle — red — and — one — bottle — water.

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: I don't like meat. Do you have vegetable dishes?
lines.literal: I — meat — not — is-loved-by-me. vegetables — you-pl-have?

lines.speaker: მიმტანი:
lines.id: Of course. Lobio, eggplant, fresh herbs.
lines.literal: what — saying — needed. lobio, eggplant, herbs.

lines.speaker: ლევანი:
lines.id: Ani, khinkali are eaten by hand, not with a fork.
lines.literal: Ani, khinkali — hand-with — is-eaten, not — fork-with.

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: By hand? In Indonesia we eat with our hands too!

lines.speaker: ნინო:
lines.id: And you don't eat the top knot — it stays on the plate.
lines.literal: and — tail — not — is-eaten — plate-on — stays.

lines.speaker: ანი:
lines.id: Got it! It's delicious. I like the lobio too.

notes: **მიყვარს and მომწონს both mean "like", but they can't be swapped.** **მიყვარს** = love, a deep and lasting liking: *ხინკალი მიყვარს* (I love khinkali — in general, for a long time). **მომწონს** = like right now, a judgment about something in front of you: *ეს ლობიო მომწონს* (I like this lobio). ⚠️ For people, მიყვარს means real love; if you've just met someone and say *შენ მიყვარხარ*, you're declaring your love.
**Both are inverted verbs**, in the same family as მაქვს and მინდა: მიყვარს (I like) / გიყვარს (you like) / უყვარს (he/she likes); მომწონს / მოგწონს / მოსწონს.
**ხელით = by hand, ჩანგლით = with a fork.** The same -ით ending from unit 5. Notice that ჩანგალი loses its ა: ჩანგ**ლ**ით.

**ინდონეზიაშიც = ინდონეზია + ში + ც.** Three endings stacked in one word: "in Indonesia too". Georgian loves stacking endings like this, and once you get used to unpacking them from the back, words that looked scary become easy to read.

**Eating khinkali has rules, and Georgians love teaching them.** Hold it by the top (კუდი, "tail"), bite a little hole in the side, slurp the broth first, then eat the rest. The top knot is **not** eaten and is left on the plate — that's also how people count how many you've had. ⚠️ Using a knife and fork on khinkali isn't a crime, but everyone at the table will notice.
**კეთილი იყოს მობრძანება = welcome.** The formal phrase written on restaurant doors and at airports. Just recognize it; you don't need to say it.
**გაუმარჯოს! = cheers.** Same root as გამარჯობა — "victory". Unit 19 explores the whole world that stands behind this word.

grammars.title: Likes, dislikes, and restrictions
after: ⚠️ If you don't eat pork — for religious or any other reasons — learn **ღორის ხორცს არ ვჭამ** as a whole: pork (ღორი) is widely used in Georgian cooking, often inside mixed-meat ხინკალი. A shorter safety phrase: *ღორი არ შეიძლება* (no pork). Beef and lamb are easy to find, and most Georgian vegetable dishes — ლობიო, ფხალი, ბადრიჯანი — contain no meat at all.

after: Two words that help at the table: **ცხარე** (tskhare, spicy) and **მარილიანი** (mariliani, salty). Georgian food is generally mild — what's called ცხარე here often just tastes pleasantly warm.

blocks.title: Six sentences for a whole dinner
items: **რას მირჩევთ?** (ras mirchevt) — What do you recommend?
**ეს რა არის?** — What's this? (unit 2 comes in handy again)
**ღორის ხორცი აქვს?** — Does this have pork in it?

blocks.text: One thing to be ready for: portions in Georgian restaurants are big, and your host — or even the server — will push you to order more than you can finish. To decline politely, say *მადლობა, ეს საკმარისია* (madloba, es sak'marisia — thank you, this is enough). If you're invited by Georgians, remember this unwritten rule: a table that isn't overflowing means the host has failed, so don't take the amount of food as a sign of how much you're expected to finish.

items: I like this lobio → ეს ლობიო ____
I don't like meat → ხორცი არ ____
I like this restaurant → ეს რესტორანი ____

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: ათი ხინკალი, თუ შეიძლება. — ხორცი არ მიყვარს. — ეს ძალიან გემრიელია. — ღორის ხორცს არ ვჭამ. — ბოსტნეული გაქვთ?
მენიუ, თუ შეიძლება. — ღორის ხორცს არ ვჭამ. — ხინკალი მიყვარს. — ეს ძალიან გემრიელია! — ბოსტნეული გაქვთ? — ანგარიში, თუ შეიძლება.
